answer: Two records, not one. Under CRMarchaeo, a 'context' is an A8 Stratigraphic Unit -- a physical feature tied to a single genesis event, with P53 has former or current location, P89 falls within, P196 defines (an E92 spacetime volume) and P45 consists of all quantified as necessary on A8 or its parent S20 Rigid Physical Feature. A posthole cut in Trench 3 and a pit fill in Trench 7 cannot share one location, one genesis event or one matter-extent, so they cannot be a single A8 instance that 'turns out' to be two features -- that would break A8's own required properties, not just a naming convention. The right model is two separate stratigraphic-unit instances (the pit fill as A2 Stratigraphic Volume Unit; the posthole, depending on whether the sheet records the cut or the fill, as A3 Stratigraphic Interface or A2), each independently identified. The number clash is then purely an E42 Identifier problem, not an entity-identity problem: E42's own scope note frames uniqueness as holding 'within the context of one or more organisations' -- an organisational convention, not an ontological guarantee -- and P48 has preferred identifier is quantified (0,1:0,n), meaning the model does not forbid one identifier value being P48/P1-linked from more than one E1 entity. So keep both A8-subclass instances, give each P1/P48 '56', and if it helps, record the two original E15 Identifier Assignment acts (by the two supervisors) to document the clash itself rather than silently normalising it away. L54 is same as would be the wrong tool here: it asserts two records are the same real thing, and the trench/feature-type evidence says these are not.

rejected_alternatives.option: Single A8 instance representing both the posthole and the pit fill
rejected_alternatives.why_not: A8's necessary properties (P53 has former or current location -> E53, P89 falls within -> E53, P196 defines -> E92, P45 consists of -> E57) and its scope note tying an instance to one genesis event mean one instance cannot coherently hold two locations, two trenches and two genesis processes.

Too generic -- S20 Rigid Physical Feature (A8's parent) is subclass of both E26 and E53 specifically to add the single-genesis matter semantics that make A8 the right specialization for a 'context'; plain E53/E26 would drop that.

rejected_alternatives.option: L54 is same as, to reconcile the two card records as one entity
rejected_alternatives.why_not: L54 asserts two records co-refer to one real thing. Here the evidence (different trench, different feature type) says they are two distinct physical things that merely share a clerical number -- asserting sameness would misrepresent the record.
